So iter-1 was BOTH under-fit per-scene AND covered only 12% of the 214 slices. Measured per-scene step cost is a clean linear function of gs_n_iter: iter-1 (n_iter=150) = 42.45 s/scene -> outer-wall hit at sample 26/214 (12% coverage), SSIM 0.738335, hr=0; iter-2 (n_iter=400) = 113.0 s/scene -> outer-wall hit at sample 10/214 (4.7% coverage), SSIM 0.736981, hr=0. So per-scene quality is NOT the lever; the average is dominated by the ~95% of scenes that NEVER complete (scored at/near their FBP init). DIAGNOSTIC QUESTION for iter-3: does COVERAGE win? At gs_n_iter=60 -> per-scene = 0.2822*60 = 16.9 s -> 1080s outer wall / 16.9 = ~64/214 scenes complete (30% coverage, ~2.5x iter-1's 26, ~6.4x iter-2's 10). FALSIFIER: if average-over-214 SSIM stays ~0.74 or WORSE even at 2.5x coverage, then BOTH levers (per-scene quality AND coverage) are exhausted within the 20-min budget -> R2-Gaussian is STRUCTURALLY budget-incompatible with the 214-slice Mayo protocol -> file the quality-vs-coverage tradeoff as a documented NEGATIVE RESULT (no gs_n_iter both covers all 214 AND fits per-scene: covering all 214 in 1080s needs n_iter<=18 steps, which is a non-recon). BUDGET MATH: 64 scenes * 16.9 s = 1082s ~ the 1080s outer wall (self-truncates and scores whatever completed, exactly as iter-1/iter-2); SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, val figure excluded. val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced) per mandate; gs_n_gaussians held at 512 (<=1024 cap). TRAJECTORY: iter-1 0.7383 (26/214) -> iter-2 0.7370 (10/214) -> iter-3 predicted ~0.74-0.76 if coverage helps (64/214), or ~0.74 (structural negative) if it does not.

ONE KNOB: gs_n_iter 60->100 (the only unmapped interior point between iter-3's 60 and iter-1's 150). FAILURE MODE (now structurally established across 3 iters): R2-Gaussian is a PER-SCENE Gaussian-splatting fit (no training, no amortization) and is BUDGET-INCOMPATIBLE with the 214-slice Mayo protocol at the hard 20-min wall. The exact [fit] outer-wall scene counts from the SLURM logs: iter-1 n_iter=150 -> sample 26 (12% coverage), SSIM 0.738335; iter-2 n_iter=400 -> sample 10 (4.7%), SSIM 0.736981; iter-3 n_iter=60 -> sample 64 (30%), SSIM 0.680981. BOTH levers are now REFUTED in NUMBERS: (a) iter-2 QUALITY lever -- 2.67x more Adam steps (150->400) moved the 214-avg by -0.0001 (FLAT); (b) iter-3 COVERAGE lever -- 2.5x more completed scenes (26->64) DROPPED the 214-avg by -0.057 (0.7383->0.6810). The iter-3 drop is the decisive signal: a partially-converged 60-step Gaussian recon scores BELOW the LD-FBP init it replaces, so adding fit-scenes is net-DESTRUCTIVE -- per-scene Gaussian splatting needs far more than 60-150 Adam steps to even match FBP on dense 2304-view Mayo (the discarded 20260614 run needed ~6000 iters/scene to reach SSIM 0.89-0.92, which at 0.282 s/step is 28 min/scene -> 0 of 214 scenes fit in 20 min). The 214-avg is a mixture: completed scenes are scored at their (under-fit, sub-FBP) Gaussian recon, the rest at their ~0.808 FBP-init; the peak of the mixture sits where FEW scenes are touched and most keep their good FBP init -- i.e. near iter-1's n_iter=150 / 26 scenes (0.7383). HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): the (coverage, SSIM) curve is smooth and monotone over [60,150]; n_iter=100 -> per-scene 0.282*100 = 28.2 s -> 1080/28.2 = ~38/214 scenes -> predicted SSIM in (0.681, 0.738), strictly BELOW iter-1's 0.738. PREDICTION: SSIM <= 0.74, hr 0. FALSIFIER: if n_iter=100 BEATS 0.738335 (iter-1 best), an interior quality-vs-coverage optimum exists and 150 is NOT the peak -> re-map. If n_iter=100 lands in (0.681, 0.738) as predicted, NO gs_n_iter beats 0.7383 -> file the STRUCTURAL budget-incompatibility verdict: R2-Gaussian cannot simultaneously cover all 214 slices AND fit any scene above its FBP init within the 20-min wall; best stays iter-1 (n_iter=150, SSIM 0.7383, hr=0, BELOW the 0.808 LD-FBP baseline). BUDGET MATH: 38 scenes * 28.2 s = 1072s ~ the 1080s outer wall (self-truncates and scores whatever completed, exactly as iter-1/2/3); SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, val figure excluded. val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced) per mandate; gs_n_gaussians held at 512 (<=1024 cap). TRAJECTORY: iter-2 0.7370 (10/214) -> iter-1 0.7383 (26/214, BEST) -> iter-4 predicted ~0.71-0.73 (38/214) -> iter-3 0.6810 (64/214). Monotone-decreasing in coverage -> R2-Gaussian is STRUCTURALLY budget-incompatible with the 214-slice Mayo protocol (documented NEGATIVE RESULT).

The gs_n_iter axis is fully mapped and its optimum is iter-1 (n_iter=150, 26/214 scenes, SSIM 0.7383, BEST). BOTH gs_n_iter levers REFUTED in numbers: QUALITY (iter-2 150->400 steps = -0.0001 FLAT) and COVERAGE-via-fewer-steps (iter-3 26->64 scenes = -0.057 DESTRUCTIVE, because a 60-step per-scene Gaussian recon scores BELOW the 0.808 LD-FBP init it replaces). gs_n_iter cannot decouple coverage from quality (cutting steps cuts quality). gs_n_gaussians is the UNTRIED axis that attacks the binding limiter (per-scene step COST = 0.282 s/step at 512 Gaussians, dominated by the dense rasterization + one 2304-view forward/back-proj) WITHOUT touching the 150-step per-scene budget that produced the BEST result. FALSIFIER: if SSIM <= 0.7383 (no lift over iter-1 best), the coverage-at-fixed-150-step-quality axis is exhausted -> r2gaussian is STRUCTURALLY budget-incompatible with the 214-slice Mayo protocol (documented NEGATIVE RESULT, hr 0): no (gs_n_iter, gs_n_gaussians) both covers all 214 AND fits any scene above its FBP init in 20 min. PREDICTION: SSIM ~0.68-0.73, hr 0 (the 150-step per-scene Gaussian recon is itself sub-FBP, so doubling coverage of sub-FBP recons most likely DROPS the avg toward 0.681 -- the structural ceiling). BUDGET MATH: ~24 s/scene x 45 scenes = ~1080s ~ the gs_outer_wall_s=1080 in-solver wall (self-truncates, scores whatever completed, exactly as iters 1-4); SLURM --time=00:30:00 default has headroom (~1100-1140s observed elapsed_s, val figure excluded). val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced) per mandate; gs_n_gaussians 256 well within the <=1024 cap. TRAJECTORY: iter-2 0.7370 (10/214) -> iter-1 0.7383 (26/214, BEST, 512 Gaussians) -> iter-3 0.6810 (64/214) | iter-5 = ~45/214 at 256 Gaussians, the coverage-at-fixed-quality test of the structural-ceiling verdict.

r2gaussian-claude-agentic: val_n=214, gs_n_gaussians=512, gs_n_iter=150, gs_lr_pos=0.005, gs_lr_scale=0.01, gs_lr_amp=0.01, gs_lr_rot=0.01, gs_amp_init=0.01, gs_scale_init=0.04, gs_tv_weight=0.0001, gs_n_clip=0.05, gs_render=raster, gs_init_from_fbp=True, gs_amp_init_max=0.05, gs_ssim_weight=0.1, gs_outer_wall_s=1080, rationale=iter-6 (search-20260619-01) PAPER-FIDELITY AUDIT FOLLOW-UP. The directive (a) was to implement the paper's radiative splat-to-detector renderer + Eq.7 rectification. FEASIBILITY VERDICT (in solver FAITHFUL_SPLAT_VERDICT): NOT a tractable net-positive iter here. (i) Rectification is a NO-OP for our forward model -- our solver rasterises the Gaussian mixture into a mu-image then applies PYRO-NN's EXACT discrete X-ray transform (unbiased line integral, no per-Gaussian normalization to omit); Zha's bias only arises in the splat-AND-SUM path, so raster-then-project ALREADY IS the unbiased operator the rectification recovers. (ii) A true 2D fan-beam splatter does NOT reuse PYRO-NN (which exposes only image<->sino on a fixed grid, no per-Gaussian detector-footprint primitive) and needs a custom differentiable EWA kernel -- hundreds of lines, far over the ~150-line one-iter bar. (iii) DECISIVE: the binding constraint is COMPUTE, not fidelity -- iters 1-5 (all hr=0, SSIM 0.68-0.74, all BELOW the 0.808 LD-FBP baseline) show the raster forward already costs ~0.282 s/Adam-step and only 10-64 of 214 slices complete in the 20-min wall; a per-Gaussian-per-view splatter is MORE expensive, so a faithful renderer would cover FEWER scenes and score WORSE. R2Gaussian is regime-bounded on dense 2304-view Mayo (hr~0 regardless); its real payoff is the 128-view SPARSE benchmarks. So I SCAFFOLDED gs_render=splat (config-gated, default raster, raises NotImplementedError) + wrote the verdict, and as the ACTUAL iter-6 take the directive's queued CHEAP in-budget lever (the iter+2 fix (b)): enable gs_init_from_fbp=True (was disabled) + add an SSIM loss term (gs_ssim_weight=0.1; benchmark is SSIM-scored). ONE COMPOUND LEVER from iter-1 BEST base (n_iter=150 / 512 Gaussians -- the config that produced the run-best SSIM 0.7383). FAILURE MODE iters 1-5: cold uniform-init Gaussians spend the scarce ~26 completed-scene budget refining a per-scene recon that lands BELOW its 0.808 FBP init, so the 214-average is dragged down by sub-FBP completed scenes. HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): FBP warm-start (positions sampled proportional to fbp^2, amp seeded from FBP intensity) + an SSIM pull toward the FBP structure makes the ~26 completed scenes land AT/ABOVE their FBP init instead of below it, so the 214-avg rises toward the 0.808 FBP baseline (from iter-1 0.7383). PREDICTION: SSIM in (0.74, 0.81), hr most likely still 0 (regime-bounded: even matching FBP yields hr=0, and beating dense-Mayo FBP per-scene in 150 Adam steps is implausible). FALSIFIER: if SSIM <= 0.7383 (no lift over iter-1 best), warm-start+SSIM does not rescue the per-scene quality and the dense-Mayo structural ceiling stands -- file the negative result. BUDGET: gs_init_from_fbp adds ~0 per-step cost (init only); the SSIM term adds one cheap conv-SSIM per step vs the dominating 2304-view projection, so per-step stays ~0.282 s and coverage ~26/214 (same as iter-1); gs_outer_wall_s=1080 self-truncates before the SLURM kill, figure excluded, --time=00:30:00 has headroom. val_n stays 214 per mandate; staged_canonical/v3/per-sample-ps(single-val-ps probe)/bg_target=truth/321px-FOV-default all hard-wired. TRAJECTORY: iter-1 0.7383 (cold, 26/214, BEST) -> iter-6 = warm FBP-init + SSIM at the SAME quality/coverage point, the fidelity-clean test of whether warm-start lifts the dense-Mayo ceiling.

TRAJECTORY: iter-1 0.7383 (cold/L2) -> iter-6 0.7519 (warm FBP-init + SSIM@0.1, BEST) -> iter-7 = SSIM weight 0.1->0.15, the does-MORE-SSIM-help test of the authorized audit-fix (b).
